prompt:
Image 1 is a finished game sprite sheet whose drawing is right: keep exactly its camera (high above, looking down at about 40 degrees), the direction every figure faces, every figure's pose, outline, size and position in its cell, the grid, and the flat pure magenta background.
Images 2 and 3 are painted portraits from the same game: repaint every figure of Image 1 in their hand. Do not copy their dark backgrounds, their candlelight, their framing or the people in them.

Repaint every figure of Image 1, a Thornwood wolf rider and his huge grey timber wolf as painterly oil on a wood panel: visible directional brushwork, a muted earthy palette of charcoal, ash grey, dull iron with rusted edges, leather and bone in which the side's deep pine-green cloth is the one clear hue; soft painterly edges with small crisp highlights on metal and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. Outdoor daylight from the upper left, a cool fill on the lower right, no cast shadows. Not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick outlines, no glossy 3D render.

The rider and his wolf, the same in every cell: A Wolf Rider: the rider in bark armor under a hooded cloak of clear deep pine green (#1F6A50), hood up, the cloak spread over his shoulders, back and the wolf's hindquarters, a pine-green tabard over his chest, and a spear with a leaf-shaped head. The mount: a huge grey timber wolf, its shoulder as high as a man's chest, shaggy grey-brown fur darker along the spine, a large pine-green saddle blanket edged with bark-brown leather that covers its back from the shoulders to the hips and hangs low on both flanks under a small bark saddle, and a pine-green quilted cloth bib over its chest under a narrow bark-plate harness. The green is a clean, clearly coloured mid-dark pine green, never blackish, olive or grey, so the rider reads as his side from far away.

Detail: at full size each figure is a finished small painting, not a flat icon: overlapping bark plates, shaggy fur with brushed locks, leather straps and buckles, cloth folds and frayed hems, a worn wooden spear shaft and a leaf-shaped iron head; varied, visible brush strokes. The values stay simple enough that the figure reads at 40 pixels: a light top (helm, shoulders, cloth) against darker legs.

Changes to make while repainting: make the rider's hood, cloak and tabard, the saddle blanket and the wolf's chest cloth a clean, clearly coloured deep pine green (#1F6A50), large and unbroken; paint the wolf's fur as thick, shaggy, brushed grey-brown fur

Facing, again: every figure in every one of the cells faces the same way, toward us and to the lower left, including the figure that is hit and the falling one; the fleeing figures alone turn away.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor or shadow; no magenta, pink or purple anywhere on the figures. Never: text, labels, grid lines, borders, a floor, cast shadows, blood, extra people, cropped or overlapping figures.
